Hey everyone, the RPC Standards team has recently merged a versioning scheme for the execution-apis repo (PR #704: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/704). The scheme uses semver to give client developers a stable target so that new spec changes don't immediately break hive rpc-compat tests.


This currently covers repo/spec versioning, but we're now exploring whether we should also introduce endpoint-level versioning for the JSON-RPC API itself. This is where wallet teams are directly impacted any versioning at the endpoint level will affect how wallets discover and interact with RPC methods.

We'd love input from wallet developers on:
1. Would endpoint versioning (e.g. /v1/, /v2/) be useful for your workflows, or does it add unnecessary complexity?
2. How do you currently handle breaking changes when the spec updates? What's your pain point?
3. Are there specific methods or response fields where backward compatibility is critical for your wallet?

Full context and discussion: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/704

We also plan to start an EthMagicians thread for longer-form discussion and invite anyone interested to join our bi-weekly RPC Standards calls (Mondays, 15:00 UTC). Happy to answer any questions!

I know it is very last minute, but would it be possible to have a few minutes to share EIP-8105 and get feedback/question on the AllWalletDevs call on Feb 18? 

Shutter recently proposed EIP-8105 (Universal Enshrined Encrypted Mempool) as a headliner for the Hegotá hardfork: 
https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8105.

I think wallet devs would be interested in helping shape EIP-8105 so it addresses their needs once implemented.
